tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

completion_summary.description: Write a headline for the observed outcome in three to six words total. Start with a past-tense verb and name the result in plain language, as in 'Booked a plumber for Thursday' or 'Renewed vehicle registration'. Leave identifiers, values, and explanations for the reply.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

This skill enforces restrained composition, image-led hierarchy, cohesive content structure, and tasteful motion while avoiding generic cards, weak branding, and UI clutter. --- # Frontend Skill Use this skill when the quality of the work depends on art direction, hierarchy, restraint, imagery, and motion rather than component count. Goal: ship interfaces that feel deliberate, premium, and current. Default toward award-level composition: one big idea, strong imagery, sparse copy, rigorous spacing, and a small number of memorable motions. ## Working Model Before building, write three things: - visual thesis: one sentence describing mood, material, and energy - content plan: hero, support, detail, final CTA - interaction thesis: 2-3 motion ideas that change the feel of the page Each section gets one job, one dominant visual idea, and one primary takeaway or action. ## Beautiful Defaults - Start with composition, not components. - Prefer a full-bleed hero or full-canvas visual anchor. - Make the brand or product name the loudest text. - Keep copy short enough to scan in seconds. - Use whitespace, alignment, scale, cropping, and contrast before adding chrome. - Limit the system: two typefaces max, one accent color by default. - Default to cardless layouts. Use sections, columns, dividers, lists, and media blocks instead. - Treat the first viewport as a poster, not a document. ## Landing Pages Default sequence: 1. Hero: brand or product, promise, CTA, and one dominant visual 2. Support: one concrete feature, offer, or proof point 3. Detail: atmosphere, workflow, product depth, or story 4. Final CTA: convert, start, visit, or contact Hero rules: - One composition only. - Full-bleed image or dominant visual plane. - Canonical full-bleed rule: on branded landing pages, the hero itself must run edge-to-edge with no inherited page gutters, framed container, or shared max-width; constrain only the inner text/action column. - Brand first, headline second, body third, CTA fourth. - No hero cards, stat strips, logo clouds, pill soup, or floating dashboards by default. - Keep headlines to roughly 2-3 lines on desktop and readable in one glance on mobile. - Keep the text column narrow and anchored to a calm area of the image. - All text over imagery must maintain strong contrast and clear tap targets. If the first viewport still works after removing the image, the image is too weak. If the brand disappears after hiding the nav, the hierarchy is too weak. Viewport budget: - If the first screen includes a sticky/fixed header, that header counts against the hero. The combined header + hero content must fit within the initial viewport at common desktop and mobile sizes. - When using `100vh`/`100svh` heroes, subtract persistent UI chrome (`calc(100svh - header-height)`) or overlay the header instead of stacking it in normal flow. ## Apps Default to Linear-style restraint: - calm surface hierarchy - strong typography and spacing - few colors - dense but readable information - minimal chrome - cards only when the card is the interaction For app UI, organize around: - primary workspace - navigation - secondary context or inspector - one clear accent for action or state Avoid: - dashboard-card mosaics - thick borders on every region - decorative gradients behind routine product UI - multiple competing accent colors - ornamental icons that do not improve scanning If a panel can become plain layout without losing meaning, remove the card treatment. ## Imagery Imagery must do narrative work. - Use at least one strong, real-looking image for brands, venues, editorial pages, and lifestyle products. - Prefer in-situ photography over abstract gradients or fake 3D objects. - Choose or crop images with a stable tonal area for text. - Do not use images with embedded signage, logos, or typographic clutter fighting the UI. - Do not generate images with built-in UI frames, splits, cards, or panels. - If multiple moments are needed, use multiple images, not one collage. The first viewport needs a real visual anchor. Decorative texture is not enough. ## Copy - Write in product language, not design commentary. - Let the headline carry the meaning. - Supporting copy should usually be one short sentence. - Cut repetition between sections. - Do not include prompt language or design commentary into the UI. - Give every section one responsibility: explain, prove, deepen, or convert. If deleting 30 percent of the copy improves the page, keep deleting. ## Utility Copy For Product UI When the work is a dashboard, app surface, admin tool, or operational workspace, default to utility copy over marketing copy. - Prioritize orientation, status, and action over promise, mood, or brand voice. - Start with the working surface itself: KPIs, charts, filters, tables, status, or task context. Do not introduce a hero section unless the user explicitly asks for one. - Section headings should say what the area is or what the user can do there. - Good: "Selected KPIs", "Plan status", "Search metrics", "Top segments", "Last sync". - Avoid aspirational hero lines, metaphors, campaign-style language, and executive-summary banners on product surfaces unless specifically requested. - Supporting text should explain scope, behavior, freshness, or decision value in one sentence. - If a sentence could appear in a homepage hero or ad, rewrite it until it sounds like product UI. - If a section does not help someone operate, monitor, or decide, remove it. - Litmus check: if an operator scans only headings, labels, and numbers, can they understand the page immediately? ## Motion Use motion to create presence and hierarchy, not noise. Ship at least 2-3 intentional motions for visually led work: - one entrance sequence in the hero - one scroll-linked, sticky, or depth effect - one hover, reveal, or layout transition that sharpens affordance Prefer Framer Motion when available for: - section reveals - shared layout transitions - scroll-linked opacity, translate, or scale shifts - sticky storytelling - carousels that advance narrative, not just fill space - menus, drawers, and modal presence effects Motion rules: - noticeable in a quick recording - smooth on mobile - fast and restrained - consistent across the page - removed if ornamental only ## Hard Rules - No cards by default. - No hero cards by default. - No boxed or center-column hero when the brief calls for full bleed. - No more than one dominant idea per section. - No section should need many tiny UI devices to explain itself. - No headline should overpower the brand on branded pages. - No filler copy. - No split-screen hero unless text sits on a calm, unified side. - No more than two typefaces without a clear reason. - No more than one accent color unless the product already has a strong system. ## Reject These Failures - Generic SaaS card grid as the first impression - Beautiful image with weak brand presence - Strong headline with no clear action - Busy imagery behind text - Sections that repeat the same mood statement - Carousel with no narrative purpose - App UI made of stacked cards instead of layout ## Litmus Checks - Is the brand or product unmistakable in the first screen? - Is there one strong visual anchor? - Can the page be understood by scanning headlines only? - Does each section have one job? - Are cards actually necessary? - Does motion improve hierarchy or atmosphere? - Would the design still feel premium if all decorative shadows were removed? # 开发协作约定

这些约定适用于整个仓库。用户在当前会话中的明确指令优先；子目录存在更具体的约定时，同时遵循适用的目录约定。

# FORGE desktop

React 18、Tauri 2、TypeScript、Vite 与单文件纯 CSS。保留每个工作空间的一条长期对话：Router 负责协调，Worker 使用私有执行上下文，后台任务和交付回到同一条对话。

```powershell
npm test
npm run build
npm run dev -- --port 5173
```

没有新增应用依赖。原生调试沿用现有 Core runtime 设置；当前锁定 Rust 依赖在本机使用已安装的 Rust 1.90 验证。Git 变更预览需要 PATH 中存在 Git。

## 导航、任务与设置

普通布局使用 52px 图标栏＋288px 项目面板，顶部页面内缩 8px、右/下边距 4px。HTML 保留 16px rem 基准，UI 使用独立 14px 字号，因此原生 `--spacing:.25rem` 正确解析为 4px。当前真实工作空间作为可展开项目，只有一个对话入口。设置、任务、记忆和收起模式仅保留图标栏；Ctrl+, 打开设置。当前没有跨空间切换接口，空间菜单只显示当前目录。

后台任务按明确的 project/workspace ID、路径或 metadata 归属分组；缺省归当前工作空间，不从任务名称猜项目。同名但不同 ID 的项目保持独立。组内需处理、运行任务优先，已结束任务默认折叠；支持搜索项目名称/路径/任务、筛选与键盘导航。计数仅表示已加载记录，轮询保留选择、折叠和滚动。

`/api/settings` 与任务读取提供 version 1 的 `project_context`：当前 workspace 的 ID、名称、根目录及默认项目键，明确 `scope=current_workspace`。侧栏与任务共用 `projectContext.ts`，同时解析 Core 实际存储的 JSON 字符串 metadata 与对象。metadata 仅用于分组，不授予目录权限；契约明确不支持跨空间切换或项目 CRUD。

设置按现有功能分为三组七项：常规、键盘快捷键、模型库、运行配置、用量与预算、供应商凭据、备份与恢复。分类栏 288px；按原生 jxU8/AWNZ/b5fQ 调用链移植，内容列最大 768px（含内部 20px 边距），导航行 30px、实际标签 14px/21px，设置行标签 13px/18.5714px、说明 12px/16px。表单选择原生 compact 输入与 md 按钮变体，28px 高、13px 字号；不同原生变体并非都为 28px。设置组使用 1px 边框、16px 圆角，支持 superellipse 时为 20px。参考 DSH 的配置层级，模型列表首层只显示名称、供应商、模型 ID、启用状态和编辑入口；能力、价格、测量和技术记录放在详情中。新档案自动生成 ID，评分与能力声明按需展开，未知值不推断为支持。

运行配置同页提供供应商连接、Router 与 API Key；已有连接的标识和能力声明默认折叠，首次启用且缺少必填标识时自动展开。预算、并发和网络范围在高级设置中。配置与密钥仍分别保存：配置保持版本确认，保存密钥沿用系统凭据库及重启流程；“检查是否存在”只检查本机凭据，不冒充模型连接测试。旧“供应商凭据”入口继续可用。API Key 仅存于密码输入控件，既不进入配置 JSON，也不进入浏览器存储。

## 对话与文件工作区

聊天默认最大 736px 居中，16px/24px 用户气泡与助手正文。输入栏按原生放在滚动区底部的绝对定位层，通过 ResizeObserver 实测高度预留阅读空间，空白层允许指针穿透。输入框不再常驻路径和变更条；对话文件计数移到 Worker 浮层。普通后台任务默认折叠为计数，审批和需要处理的任务直接可见。21px 活动摘要逐层展开，技术字段收在记录详情；失败、未知与模拟标记独立显示，长命令不能裁掉风险信息。不生成思考正文或时长。

命令卡按原始桌面 bundle 实现 Shell 标题、命令/输出分别复制、144px 输出独立滚动、右下真实退出状态；圆角 12.5px、边框 0.8px，长命令可完整展开。文件写入/修订展开后直接读取精确不可变回执，在会话内显示路径、增删数和 diff，不必先打开右栏。diff 为 12px/21.6px、单行号、4px 红绿色条与整行底色，最大高 240px；原/新行号来自实际 unified diff hunk。折叠时不读取，展开后在内存保留回执及双轴阅读位置，轮询和活动拆组不重置；连接/空间/代次变化清除缓存。完整历史入口继续保留。

活动组中真实成功的写入/修订按路径去重，默认显示 3 个文件，可展开更多并预览；刷新与重分组保留展开和阅读锚点。Worker 的独立执行详情按 run ID 匹配，显示真实角色、模型、状态及已记录步数/工具次数，历史事件与最新执行状态区分；记录未加载时明确提示。

工具栏的文件按钮，或对话里的文件引用，可打开右侧预览。文档在左、文件树在右；树内同时提供已更改目录与所有文件，过滤针对已加载文件，状态来自真实 Git。支持文件标签、面包屑、预览/源码切换、键盘切换/关闭、可拖动和键盘调整的分隔条、独立滚动及刷新。展开按钮可将预览扩展为完整文件工作区，保留聊天 DOM、草稿和阅读位置。开合继续使用用户要求的 150ms 宽度/透明度过渡，退出保留文档 DOM 并禁用隐藏控件，支持快速反向切换与减少动效。窗口缩放按原生 Root.H/Kg/g3 的断点变化收起/恢复右栏：工作区（含可见左导航）跨到 960px 以下且项目栏打开，或跨到 720px 以下时收起，放宽后恢复一次；手动开关清除恢复记录，连续更窄的断点按原文覆盖当时开关状态。展开意图、文件标签和滚动继续保留。FORGE 没有原生的 route/owner lease/tab retain 特例；720px 以下主动打开文件仍为全宽单面板，水平导航也是 FORGE 适配。

预览宽度直接移植原生 DUYS 的默认值和归一化比例算法。以实际主区宽 W 和 workspace 行高 H 计算 `max(320,min(1.6H,W−500),min(640,W−352))`，regular 区间为 320 至 `max(320,W−352)`。首个真实测量后冻结比例，窗口缩放继续使用同一比例；展开时全宽，恢复后沿用原比例。分隔器覆盖布局，不占额外列宽；双击恢复当前默认宽，拖到 160px 以下关闭，越界至聊天不足 160px 时展开。移除了此前 660px/41–64%、1424px 自动收栏和 1136px 单面板的自行校准规则。

文件树按原生 U5mJ/gbrq 共用一个初始 250px 宽度，夹在 200px 与父宽 60% 之间，CSS 额外限制 max-width 60%。左边缘可拖动，拖至 100px 以下隐藏；普通与完整工作区共享该状态。为支持现有“文件”入口，FORGE 的文件请求仍自动显示树。普通与展开状态采用 14px 标签/操作文字、13px 文件名、30px 树行、16px 文件图标、48px 文件工具栏。BaseFileTree 的实际覆盖为横向 padding 3px、gap 5px、层级间距 8.75px；移植 20 类 DMvp 内联文件 SVG、目录 chevron、悬停层级线和 20px 状态框。新增/修改/删除分别为原生 sectioned 树的 #00a240/#0285ff/#e02e2a，普通选中文字为正文色。原增删计数保留在无障碍文本中。

文件树开关位于工具栏最右侧，标签栏的“＋”使用现有文件选择能力：浏览器打开文件选择器，原生展开目录树并聚焦过滤。源码查找默认收起，通过“查找文件内容”或源码区 Ctrl+F 展开；Enter/Shift+Enter 定位，Escape 关闭并回到源码。窄预览在 560px 以下将工具栏文字折为图标，保留原可访问名称；这些入口安排是结合用户截图的 FORGE 适配，未增加原应用专属的编辑器启动接口。

- 源码：只读、行号、基本词法着色、按需展开的查找、复制、横向滚动/换行。非换行视图虚拟化；超过 5000 行关闭换行，避免长文件拖慢界面。
- Markdown：16px/24px 正文，文档内边距 12px 16px；预览/源码切换保留阅读位置，相对链接打开同空间文件。HTML 不执行，外链图片不加载，危险 URL 不渲染。
- PDF：使用实际读取字节创建并回收 Blob URL，交给内置查看器提供多页、缩放、查找和页面适配；不支持内嵌时提供明确说明与下载。
- Git：显示当前工作空间的真实变更与差异，支持子目录、重命名、删除、新文件、无 HEAD 仓库；工作树与 HEAD 相同但暂存区有修改时明确显示暂存差异。Git 读取不写索引。
- 工作空间变更与对话文件记录分别标明口径；对话汇总仅含已加载记录中真实成功的文件写入。
- 历史更改：展开成功文件写入/修订记录后选择“记录的更改”，按精确工具回执读取历史 diff、增删数与基础版本。历史标签与当前文件标签独立；相同文件的多个回执可并排切换。加载后增删数回填对应活动行。刷新、关闭重开保留阅读位置，连接/空间/代次变化清除旧内容。

历史数据由独立认证只读接口 `GET /api/artifacts/receipts/{receipt_id}/diff` 提供，验证完整执行/版本回执链，使用不可变 `action_intents` 中保存的正文，绝不以当前文件或 Git 补作历史基线。单版本上限 256 KiB/2000 行，最多 64 个版本、累计 4 MiB，diff 上限 512 KiB；过大返回 422，不可用/敏感路径/损坏回执返回不含内部细节的 404。模拟来源始终标注。来源跳转表示“关联任务的请求”，不证明该请求直接导致每个历史 run；未加载消息有明确提示，不冒充精确聊天轮次归属。

浏览器开发模式点击“文件”，选择本地目录或文件；不会把浏览器测试数据当作工作空间文件。目录导入移除共同顶层目录，保留相对文件引用。导入文件没有 Git 历史。

# FORGE v4 — General-purpose Super-agent

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose DeepSeek-style Super-agent desktop
application: one persistent Router conversation coordinates hidden, isolated
Workers and continuously receives events.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-16

The backend architecture now follows DeepSeek Super-agent's
persistent Router and independent Workers. The default Core delegates ordinary
conversational tasks automatically, filters environmental events, sends Thread
continuations directly to subscribed Workers, follows typed Chain of Recall
references, and supervises durable execution. Plans, Quests and approval records
are internal infrastructure. The frontend is unchanged in this correction.

Read the [architecture audit and refactor plan](docs/SUPERAGENT_REFACTOR_PLAN.md),
[product architecture](docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[implementation and validation report](docs/SUPERAGENT_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md)
for the exact implemented behavior, tests, real Provider observations and limits.
Historical Phase 2 evidence remains available below; it does not describe the
new autonomous dispatch path.

Frozen-source real Provider acceptance passed both the
[conversational/restart scenario](docs/audit/superagent/20261115T193658Z-d72209.json)
and the [event/adaptive-team scenario](docs/audit/superagent/20261115T193938Z-cold-697d50.json),
with 22/22 and 17/17 calls settled respectively. These bounded observations
verify the new backend flow; exact tool limits and regression debt are recorded
in the implementation report and do not establish arbitrary-task correctness.
The frozen backend regression recorded **2312 passed, 14 failed, 2 skipped**;
the fourteen failures match those reproduced on the base source and tests.
See the [acceptance index](docs/audit/superagent/acceptance-index.json) for
report hashes, final evidence and preserved diagnostic history.

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [V22 historical boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v22-boundary.md).
Historical failures and original evidence remain preserved. The real algorithm
microstudy scored 25/90 task successes; it does not establish general policy gains.
Frontend work is being handled separately; packaging is outside this sprint.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. DeepSeek Super-agent defines the overall architecture; Codex and Claude Code inform Harness design. None is an execution backend.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering implementation with bounded context recovery, source-bound
recall and evidence-gated execution. A configured Provider is required; Mock
tests and real Provider observations are identified separately. Autonomous
internal plan/team contracts use an auditable host mandate tied to the original
request or admitted Trigger. Manual approvals retain authenticated user authority,
and risky tool actions still require their own authorization. A mandate or
proposal does not prove execution. Worker directories are private execution
contexts, not an OS sandbox. General complex-task correctness remains subject to
recorded acceptance.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

"""Small reproducible capability probes, not general intelligence ratings.

Each dimension has one public fixed case and a deterministic oracle. Reports
retain hashes and measured usage, never promote a single success to Registry
capability scores. Visual ability remains unsupported by this text-only suite.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import time

from .code_test_harness import HarnessError, run_tests
from .domain import new_id, now_iso
from .model_performance import _rate
from .runtime import ModelCallContext, ModelRequest
from .worker_recovery import provider_failure_code

SUITE_VERSION = "forge-capability-micro-v1"
PROBES = {
    "mathematics": (
        "Return JSON only: {\"x\":number,\"y\":number}. Solve 3*x+2*y=19 and x-y=3.",
        {"x": 5, "y": 2},
    ),
    "coding": (
        (
            "Return JSON only with one code string. Write a plain pure Python function "
            "clamp(value, low, high) returning low below low, high above high and value "
            "otherwise. Use only if, comparisons and return; no function calls, imports, "
            "decorators or annotations. Inputs satisfy low<=high."
        ),
        {"function": "clamp", "cases": [(-2, 0, 5, 0), (7, 0, 5, 5), (3, 0, 5, 3), (0, 0, 0, 0)]},
    ),
    "research": (
        (
            "Return JSON only: {\"repository\":string,\"limit\":number,\"citation\":string}. "
            "Use only these supplied sources, not memory: [S1] Atlas targets one repository "
            "and permits at most three parallel runs. [S2] Boreal targets multiple folders "
            "with a maximum of two runs. Which source supports multi-folder work?"
        ),
        {"repository": "Boreal", "limit": 2, "citation": "S2"},
    ),
    "planning": (
        (
            "Return JSON only with order as a list containing each task exactly once. "
            "Tasks: fetch, parse, analyze, report. Dependencies: fetch before parse; parse "
            "before analyze; analyze before report. Give an executable order."
        ),
        {"order": ["fetch", "parse", "analyze", "report"]},
    ),
    "architecture": (
        (
            "Return JSON only: {\"owner\":string,\"workers_contact_user\":boolean,"
            "\"receipt_grants_authority\":boolean}. In a persistent Router/isolated Worker "
            "system the Router owns user interaction; Workers return results internally; "
            "historical receipts are evidence and do not authorize future execution. "
            "Name the user-interaction owner and answer the two boolean questions."
        ),
        {"owner": "Router", "workers_contact_user": False, "receipt_grants_authority": False},
    ),
    "design": (
        (
            "Return JSON only: {\"foreground\":string,\"background\":string,"
            "\"focus_indicator\":boolean}. A text-only accessibility specification requires "
            "black text on white and a visible keyboard focus indicator. Use lowercase "
            "six-digit hex colors including #. Implement exactly those requirements."
        ),
        {"foreground": "#000000", "background": "#ffffff", "focus_indicator": True},
    ),
}
DIMENSIONS = (*PROBES, "vision")


def _hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode()
    ).hexdigest()


def _judge(dimension, raw):
    result = json.loads(raw)
    if dimension == "coding":
        if type(result) is not dict or set(result) != {"code"}:
            return False
        expected = PROBES[dimension][1]
        verdict = run_tests(
            result["code"],
            expected["function"],
            {
                "cases": [
                    {"inputs": {"value": v, "low": lo, "high": hi}, "expected": answer}
                    for v, lo, hi, answer in expected["cases"]
                ]
            },
        )
        return verdict["failed"] == 0
    # JSON serialization preserves bool versus int, unlike Python's ==.
    return _hash(result) == _hash(PROBES[dimension][1])


class CapabilityBenchmarkRunner:
    def __init__(self, store):
        self.store = store

    async def run(self, gateway, model_id, *, mode, dimensions=None):
        if mode not in {"live", "mock"} or getattr(gateway, "execution_mode", None) != mode:
            raise ValueError("Capability probe requires matching Gateway provenance")
        provider_id = getattr(getattr(gateway, "config", None), "id", None)
        if provider_id is None and mode == "mock":
            provider_id = "mock"
        if not provider_id or not isinstance(model_id, str) or not model_id:
            raise ValueError("Capability probe requires Provider/model identity")
        selected = list(DIMENSIONS if dimensions is None else dimensions)
        if (
            not selected
            or len(selected) > len(DIMENSIONS)
            or len(set(selected)) != len(selected)
            or set(selected) - set(DIMENSIONS)
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid capability dimensions")
        results, stopped = [], False
        for dimension in selected:
            if dimension == "vision" or stopped:
                results.append(
                    {
                        "dimension": dimension,
                        "status": "unsupported" if dimension == "vision" else "not_attempted",
                        "passed": None,
                        "reason_code": "text_only_suite" if dimension == "vision" else "prior_provider_failure",
                    }
                )
                continue
            prompt = "Capability microprobe " + dimension + ". " + PROBES[dimension][0]
            call_id = new_id("call")
            start = time.monotonic()
            item = {
                "dimension": dimension,
                "case_id": dimension + "-1",
                "call_id": call_id,
                "prompt_sha256": _hash(prompt),
                "oracle_sha256": _hash(PROBES[dimension][1]),
            }
            try:
                response = await gateway.generate(
                    ModelRequest(
                        model_id=model_id,
                        provider_id=provider_id,
                        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
                        max_output_tokens=512,
                        context_limit=8192,
                        max_retries=0,
                        budget_context=ModelCallContext(
                            call_id=call_id,
                            purpose="capability_benchmark",
                            workspace_id=self.store.workspace.id,
                        ),
                    )
                )
                if response.provider_id != provider_id or response.model_id != model_id:
                    raise ValueError("Capability response identity changed")
                item["response_sha256"] = _hash(response.text)
                item["usage"] = {
                    key: response.usage.get(key)
                    for key in ("input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cached_input_tokens")
                }
                try:
                    item["passed"] = (
                        not response.tool_calls
                        and response.finish_reason in {"stop", "end_turn"}
                        and len(response.text.encode("utf-8")) <= 8192
                        and _judge(dimension, response.text)
                    )
                    item["status"] = "judged"
                except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, HarnessError):
                    item.update(passed=False, status="judged", reason_code="invalid_response_contract")
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - no remote exception text or unbounded retry.
                item.update(passed=False, status="provider_failed", reason_code=provider_failure_code(exc))
                stopped = True
            item["elapsed_seconds"] = time.monotonic() - start
            results.append(item)
        identifier, created = new_id("benchmark"), now_iso()
        report = {
            "id": identifier,
            "provider_id": provider_id,
            "model_id": model_id,
            "mode": mode,
            "suite_version": SUITE_VERSION,
            "created_at": created,
            "results": results,
            "n_samples": sum(item["status"] in {"judged", "provider_failed"} for item in results),
            "limitations": "One public microcase per dimension; design tests literal accessibility requirements, not visual quality. No general capability estimate or Registry override.",
        }
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            work.connection.execute(
                "INSERT INTO benchmark_runs VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                (identifier, model_id, provider_id, SUITE_VERSION, mode, json.dumps(results), created),
            )
        return report

    def summarize(self, model_id, provider_id, *, mode="live", limit=32):
        if mode not in {"mock", "live"} or type(limit) is not int or not 1 <= limit <= 256:
            raise ValueError("Invalid capability summary bounds or provenance")
        with self.store.connection() as c:
            rows = c.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM benchmark_runs WHERE model_id=? AND provider_id=? AND mode=? "
                "AND suite_version=? ORDER BY created_at DESC,id DESC LIMIT ?",
                (model_id, provider_id, mode, SUITE_VERSION, limit + 1),
            ).fetchall()
        measured = {}
        for dimension in DIMENSIONS:
            cases = [
                item
                for row in rows[:limit]
                for item in json.loads(row["results_json"])
                if item.get("dimension") == dimension
                and item.get("status") in {"judged", "provider_failed"}
            ]
            measured[dimension] = _rate(sum(item.get("passed") is True for item in cases), len(cases))
        return {
            "provider_id": provider_id,
            "model_id": model_id,
            "execution_mode": mode,
            "source": "fixed_capability_microprobe",
            "suite_version": SUITE_VERSION,
            "measured_at": rows[0]["created_at"] if rows else None,
            "measurements": measured,
            "source_refs": ["benchmark:" + row["id"] for row in rows[:limit]],
            "sample_truncated": len(rows) > limit,
            "limitations": "Repeated fixed public cases are not independent samples of general capability; unsupported vision remains unknown.",
        }

"""Bounded Core observations, kept separate from manually supplied ability scores.

Transport success is never interpreted as task success. These snapshots describe
recorded executions, not a benchmark estimate of general model capabilities.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import math
import time


def _rate(successes, samples):
    if not samples:
        return None
    # Wilson 95% interval is intentionally wide for small samples.
    z = 1.959963984540054
    value = successes / samples
    divisor = 1 + z * z / samples
    center = (value + z * z / (2 * samples)) / divisor
    half = z * math.sqrt(value * (1 - value) / samples + z * z / (4 * samples**2)) / divisor
    return {
        "value": value,
        "n_samples": samples,
        "confidence": {
            "method": "wilson_95",
            "lower": max(0, center - half),
            "upper": min(1, center + half),
        },
    }


def performance_snapshot(connection, provider_id, model_id, *, mode="live", limit=256):
    """Read a bounded recent sample in the caller's transaction without editing profiles.

    All joins bind provider, model and execution mode. Unknown token prices,
    missing usage, task quality and schema outcomes remain unknown. Source IDs
    and a digest make the exact proposal-time snapshot auditable after restart.
    """
    if mode not in {"live", "mock"} or type(limit) is not int or not 1 <= limit <= 1024:
        raise ValueError("Invalid performance snapshot bounds or provenance")
    observations = connection.execute(
        """SELECT * FROM model_observations WHERE provider_id=? AND model_id=? AND mode=?
        ORDER BY created_at DESC,id DESC LIMIT ?""",
        (provider_id, model_id, mode, limit + 1),
    ).fetchall()
    runs = connection.execute(
        """SELECT * FROM worker_runs WHERE provider_id=? AND model_id=? AND execution_mode=?
        ORDER BY created_at DESC,id DESC LIMIT ?""",
        (provider_id, model_id, mode, limit + 1),
    ).fetchall()
    omitted = {"gateway": len(observations) > limit, "workers": len(runs) > limit}
    observations, runs = observations[:limit], runs[:limit]
    metrics = {}
    rates = {
        "transport_success_rate": _rate(
            sum(row["outcome"] == "success" for row in observations), len(observations)
        ),
        "transport_error_rate": _rate(
            sum(row["outcome"] == "error" for row in observations), len(observations)
        ),
        "transport_timeout_rate": _rate(
            sum(row["outcome"] == "timeout" for row in observations), len(observations)
        ),
        "task_success_rate": _rate(
            sum(row["state"] == "succeeded" for row in runs),
            sum(row["state"] in {"succeeded", "failed"} for row in runs),
        ),
        "worker_blocked_rate": _rate(
            sum(row["state"] == "blocked" for row in runs),
            sum(row["state"] in {"succeeded", "failed", "blocked"} for row in runs),
        ),
    }
    elapsed = sorted(
        row["latency_seconds"] for row in observations if row["latency_seconds"] is not None
    )
    if elapsed:
        metrics["average_latency_seconds"] = {
            "value": sum(elapsed) / len(elapsed),
            "n_samples": len(elapsed),
            "confidence": None,
        }
        metrics["p95_latency_seconds"] = {
            "value": elapsed[math.ceil(0.95 * len(elapsed)) - 1],
            "n_samples": len(elapsed),
            "confidence": None,
        }
    generation_rates = [
        row["output_tokens"] / (row["latency_seconds"] - row["ttft_seconds"])
        for row in observations
        if row["outcome"] == "success"
        and row["output_tokens"] is not None
        and row["ttft_seconds"] is not None
        and row["latency_seconds"] is not None
        and row["latency_seconds"] > row["ttft_seconds"]
    ]
    if generation_rates:
        metrics["tokens_per_second"] = {
            "value": sum(generation_rates) / len(generation_rates),
            "n_samples": len(generation_rates),
            "confidence": None,
            "coverage": "successful_streams_with_observed_first_token_only",
        }
    source_rows = [dict(row) for row in observations]
    source_rows.extend(dict(row) for row in runs)
    refs = [f"model_observation:{row['id']}" for row in observations]
    refs.extend(f"worker_run:{row['id']}" for row in runs)
    if runs:
        run_ids = [row["id"] for row in runs]
        worker_ids = [row["worker_id"] for row in runs]
        placeholders = ",".join("?" for _ in run_ids)
        tools = connection.execute(
            f"SELECT * FROM worker_tool_calls WHERE run_id IN ({placeholders}) ORDER BY run_id,call_id LIMIT ?",
            (*run_ids, limit + 1),
        ).fetchall()
        attempts = connection.execute(
            f"""SELECT * FROM model_budget_attempts WHERE worker_run_id IN ({placeholders})
            AND provider_id=? AND model_id=? ORDER BY created_at DESC,attempt_id DESC LIMIT ?""",
            (*run_ids, provider_id, model_id, limit + 1),
        ).fetchall()
        events = connection.execute(
            f"""SELECT * FROM events WHERE worker_id IN ({placeholders})
            AND event_type IN ('worker.result','worker.retry','worker.progress','worker.blocked','worker.failed')
            ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT ?""",
            (*worker_ids, limit + 1),
        ).fetchall()
        reviews = connection.execute(
            f"""SELECT * FROM node_verification_attempts WHERE worker_id IN ({placeholders})
            ORDER BY plan_id,node_key,worker_id LIMIT ?""",
            (*worker_ids, limit + 1),
        ).fetchall()
        verdicts = connection.execute(
            f"""SELECT * FROM events WHERE worker_id IN ({placeholders})
            AND event_type='review.result' AND json_extract(payload,'$.provider_id')=?
            AND json_extract(payload,'$.model_id')=?
            AND json_extract(payload,'$.execution_mode')=? ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT ?""",
            (*worker_ids, provider_id, model_id, mode, limit + 1),
        ).fetchall()
        omitted.update(
            {
                "tools": len(tools) > limit,
                "attempts": len(attempts) > limit,
                "events": len(events) > limit,
                "reviews": len(reviews) > limit,
                "review_verdicts": len(verdicts) > limit,
            }
        )
        verdicts = [
            row
            for row in verdicts[:limit]
            if json.loads(row["payload"]).get("run_id") in run_ids
        ]
        tools, attempts, events, reviews = (
            tools[:limit],
            attempts[:limit],
            events[:limit],
            reviews[:limit],
        )
        settled_tools = [row for row in tools if row["state"] in {"succeeded", "failed"}]
        rates["tool_call_success_rate"] = _rate(
            sum(row["state"] == "succeeded" for row in settled_tools), len(settled_tools)
        )
        settled_reviews = [row for row in reviews if row["state"] in {"verified", "blocked"}]
        rates["review_pass_rate"] = _rate(
            sum(row["state"] == "verified" for row in settled_reviews), len(settled_reviews)
        )
        judged = [
            json.loads(row["payload"])
            for row in verdicts
            if json.loads(row["payload"]).get("error_code") is None
            and json.loads(row["payload"]).get("verdict") in {"PASS", "NEEDS_REVISION", "BLOCKED"}
        ]
        rates["independent_review_verdict_pass_rate"] = _rate(
            sum(item["verdict"] == "PASS" for item in judged), len(judged)
        )
        rates["independent_review_error_rate"] = _rate(
            sum(json.loads(row["payload"]).get("error_code") is not None for row in verdicts),
            len(verdicts),
        )
        retry_workers = set()
        valid_schema = invalid_schema = retry_count = 0
        for event in events:
            payload = json.loads(event["payload"])
            if payload.get("run_id") not in run_ids:
                continue
            repair = (
                event["event_type"] == "worker.progress" and payload.get("phase") == "self_repair"
            )
            retry = event["event_type"] == "worker.retry" or repair
            if retry:
                retry_count += 1
                retry_workers.add(event["worker_id"])
            valid_schema += event["event_type"] == "worker.result"
            invalid_schema += payload.get("reason_code") == "invalid_output_contract" and (
                repair or event["event_type"] in {"worker.blocked", "worker.failed"}
            )
        rates["schema_compliance"] = _rate(valid_schema, valid_schema + invalid_schema)
        rates["retry_rate"] = _rate(len(retry_workers), len(runs))
        metrics["retry_count"] = {"value": retry_count, "n_samples": len(runs), "confidence": None}
        charged = [
            row
            for row in attempts
            if row["input_charged"] is not None and row["output_charged"] is not None
        ]
        if charged:
            metrics["token_consumption"] = {
                "value": sum(row["input_charged"] + row["output_charged"] for row in charged),
                "n_samples": len(charged),
                "confidence": None,
                "coverage": "known_charged_attempts_only",
            }
        currencies = {row["currency"] for row in charged}
        if (
            charged
            and all(row["cost_charged"] is not None for row in charged)
            and len(currencies) == 1
            and None not in currencies
        ):
            metrics["cost_microunits"] = {
                "value": sum(row["cost_charged"] for row in charged),
                "currency": next(iter(currencies)),
                "n_samples": len(charged),
                "confidence": None,
                "coverage": "known_charged_attempts_only",
            }
        refs.extend(f"worker_tool_call:{row['run_id']}:{row['call_id']}" for row in tools)
        refs.extend(f"model_attempt:{row['attempt_id']}" for row in attempts)
        refs.extend(f"event:{row['id']}" for row in events)
        refs.extend(f"event:{row['id']}" for row in verdicts)
        refs.extend(
            f"node_verification:{row['plan_id']}:{row['node_key']}:{row['worker_id']}"
            for row in reviews
        )
        for group in (tools, attempts, events, reviews, verdicts):
            source_rows.extend(dict(row) for row in group)
    metrics.update({name: value for name, value in rates.items() if value is not None})
    latest = max(
        [
            row["created_at"]
            for row in [*observations, *runs, *(events if runs else []), *(verdicts if runs else [])]
        ],
        default=None,
    )
    for measurement in metrics.values():
        measurement.update(
            source="core_execution_observation", execution_mode=mode, measured_at=latest
        )
    digest = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(source_rows, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode(
            "utf-8"
        )
    ).hexdigest()
    return {
        "provider_id": provider_id,
        "model_id": model_id,
        "execution_mode": mode,
        "source": "core_execution_observation",
        "measurements": metrics,
        "source_refs": refs[:32],
        "source_refs_omitted": max(0, len(refs) - 32),
        "snapshot_sha256": digest,
        "sample_limit": limit,
        "sample_truncated": omitted,
        "unknown_usage_attempts": sum(
            row["input_charged"] is None or row["output_charged"] is None for row in attempts
        )
        if runs
        else 0,
        "limitations": "Recent bounded execution observations; transport success is not task success; no general capability estimate.",
    }


def model_health_snapshot(
    connection, provider_id, model_id, *, mode="live", limit=32, failure_threshold=3, now=None
):
    """A sourced health signal, never authority to retry an unknown operation.

    Gateway observations carry no request ID. They establish transport health;
    unresolved accounting is therefore inspected independently through Worker-bound
    reservations with matching execution provenance, never guessed from failures.
    """
    if (
        mode not in {"live", "mock"}
        or type(limit) is not int
        or not 1 <= limit <= 256
        or type(failure_threshold) is not int
        or not 1 <= failure_threshold <= 10
        or not isinstance(provider_id, str)
        or not provider_id
        or not isinstance(model_id, str)
        or not model_id
    ):
        raise ValueError("Invalid model health bounds or identity")
    now = time.time() if now is None else now
    if type(now) not in (int, float) or not math.isfinite(now):
        raise ValueError("Invalid model health clock")
    observations = connection.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM model_observations WHERE provider_id=? AND model_id=? AND mode=? "
        "ORDER BY created_at DESC,id DESC LIMIT ?",
        (provider_id, model_id, mode, limit),
    ).fetchall()
    unknown = connection.execute(
        "SELECT s.call_id,s.run_id,s.state,r.state AS run_state,r.lease_until,r.deadline "
        "FROM worker_model_reservations s JOIN worker_runs r ON r.id=s.run_id "
        "WHERE s.provider_id=? AND s.model_id=? AND s.execution_mode=? AND s.state='reserved' "
        "ORDER BY s.created_at DESC,s.call_id DESC LIMIT ?",
        (provider_id, model_id, mode, limit + 1),
    ).fetchall()
    attempts = connection.execute(
        "SELECT a.attempt_id,a.call_id,a.worker_run_id,a.state,a.recover_after,"
        "r.state AS run_state,r.lease_until,r.deadline FROM model_budget_attempts a "
        "JOIN worker_runs r ON r.id=a.worker_run_id "
        "WHERE a.provider_id=? AND a.model_id=? AND r.execution_mode=? "
        "AND a.state IN ('reserved','overrun') ORDER BY a.created_at DESC LIMIT ?",
        (provider_id, model_id, mode, limit + 1),
    ).fetchall()
    cooldown = connection.execute(
        "SELECT retry_after FROM model_provider_cooldowns WHERE provider_id=?", (provider_id,)
    ).fetchone()
    cooling = bool(cooldown and cooldown[0] > now)
    failures = 0
    for observation in observations:
        if observation["outcome"] == "success":
            break
        failures += 1
    def in_flight(row):
        return (
            row["state"] == "reserved"
            and row["deadline"] > now
            and (
                row["run_state"] == "running"
                and row["lease_until"] is not None
                and row["lease_until"] > now
                or row["run_state"] == "review_pending"
            )
            and (
                "recover_after" not in row.keys()  # noqa: SIM118 - sqlite3.Row membership tests values.
                or row["recover_after"] is None
                or row["recover_after"] > now
            )
        )

    unknown_calls = {row["call_id"] for row in [*unknown, *attempts] if not in_flight(row)}
    in_flight_calls = {row["call_id"] for row in [*unknown, *attempts] if in_flight(row)}
    recommendation = (
        "blocked_unknown"
        if unknown_calls
        else "degraded"
        if cooling or failures >= failure_threshold
        else "available"
        if observations
        else "unknown"
    )
    sources = {
        "observations": [dict(row) for row in observations],
        "unsettled_worker_calls": [dict(row) for row in unknown],
        "unsettled_worker_attempts": [dict(row) for row in attempts],
        "cooldown": dict(cooldown) if cooldown else None,
        "failure_threshold": failure_threshold,
        "recommendation": recommendation,
    }
    refs = [f"model_observation:{row['id']}" for row in observations]
    refs.extend(f"model_call:{row['call_id']}" for row in unknown)
    refs.extend(f"model_attempt:{row['attempt_id']}" for row in attempts)
    return {
        "provider_id": provider_id,
        "model_id": model_id,
        "execution_mode": mode,
        "source": "core_execution_observation",
        "recommendation": recommendation,
        "consecutive_failures": failures,
        "failure_threshold": failure_threshold,
        "transport_failure_rate": _rate(
            sum(row["outcome"] != "success" for row in observations), len(observations)
        ),
        "transport_timeout_rate": _rate(
            sum(row["outcome"] == "timeout" for row in observations), len(observations)
        ),
        "unknown_attempts": len(unknown_calls),
        "in_flight_calls": len(in_flight_calls),
        "unknown_sample_truncated": len(unknown) > limit or len(attempts) > limit,
        "provider_cooldown_until": cooldown[0] if cooling else None,
        "source_refs": refs[:32],
        "source_refs_omitted": max(0, len(refs) - 32),
        "snapshot_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
            json.dumps(sources, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
        ).hexdigest(),
        "sample_limit": limit,
        "observed_at": observations[0]["created_at"] if observations else None,
        "limitations": "Transport health and Worker-bound unsettled accounting only; provenance of non-Worker Gateway attempts is not inferred. Not model quality or permission to replay any call.",
    }

"""Local deterministic timer and file sources, driven by the host polling loop."""

import base64
import hashlib
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path

from .domain import DomainError, new_id
from .superagent_events import TriggerService, _identifier


class LocalTriggerSources:
    def __init__(self, store, *, clock=None):
        self.store = store
        self.events = TriggerService(store, **({"clock": clock} if clock is not None else {}))
        self.clock = self.events.clock

    def _source(self, connection, source_id, kind):
        source = connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM superagent_sources WHERE id=?",
            (source_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if (
            source is None
            or source["workspace_id"] != self.store.workspace.id
            or source["kind"] != kind
        ):
            raise DomainError(f"Source is not a registered local {kind} source")
        return source

    def schedule(
        self,
        source_id,
        thread_key,
        payload,
        *,
        due_at,
        interval_seconds=None,
        actor=None,
        addressed=True,
        timer_id=None,
    ):
        _identifier(thread_key, "timer thread")
        if (
            type(due_at) not in (int, float)
            or not math.isfinite(due_at)
            or due_at < 0
            or (
                interval_seconds is not None
                and (
                    type(interval_seconds) not in (int, float)
                    or not math.isfinite(interval_seconds)
                    or interval_seconds < 1
                )
            )
            or not isinstance(payload, dict)
            or type(addressed) is not bool
        ):
            raise DomainError("Invalid timer schedule")
        if actor is not None:
            _identifier(actor, "timer actor")
        timer_id = _identifier(timer_id or new_id("timer"), "timer ID")
        try:
            encoded = json.dumps(
                payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False
            )
        except (TypeError, ValueError, RecursionError) as exc:
            raise DomainError("Timer payload must be finite JSON") from exc
        if len(encoded.encode("utf-8")) > 4 * 1024 * 1024:
            raise DomainError("Timer payload exceeds ingress limit")
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            c = work.connection
            self._source(c, source_id, "timer")
            old = c.execute("SELECT * FROM superagent_timers WHERE id=?", (timer_id,)).fetchone()
            if old:
                if tuple(
                    old[key]
                    for key in (
                        "source_id",
                        "thread_key",
                        "payload_json",
                        "actor",
                        "addressed",
                        "interval_seconds",
                    )
                ) != (source_id, thread_key, encoded, actor, int(addressed), interval_seconds):
                    raise DomainError("Timer identity conflicts with stored schedule")
                return dict(old)
            c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO superagent_timers VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,0,1)",
                (
                    timer_id,
                    source_id,
                    thread_key,
                    encoded,
                    actor,
                    int(addressed),
                    due_at,
                    interval_seconds,
                ),
            )
            return dict(
                c.execute("SELECT * FROM superagent_timers WHERE id=?", (timer_id,)).fetchone()
            )

    def poll_due(self, *, limit=32):
        if type(limit) is not int or not 1 <= limit <= 256:
            raise DomainError("Invalid timer poll limit")
        now = self.clock()
        if type(now) not in (int, float) or not math.isfinite(now):
            raise DomainError("Invalid timer clock")
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            c = work.connection
            timers = c.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM superagent_timers WHERE enabled=1 AND next_at<=? "
                "ORDER BY next_at,id LIMIT ?",
                (now, limit),
            ).fetchall()
            triggers = []
            for timer in timers:
                source = self._source(c, timer["source_id"], "timer")
                occurrence = timer["occurrence"] + 1
                triggers.append(
                    self.events.receive(
                        timer["source_id"],
                        f"{timer['id']}:{occurrence}",
                        timer["thread_key"],
                        json.loads(timer["payload_json"]),
                        actor=timer["actor"],
                        addressed=bool(timer["addressed"]),
                        conversation_id=source["conversation_id"],
                        connection=c,
                    )
                )
                interval = timer["interval_seconds"]
                # Coalesce missed periods into one event; a restart never floods
                # the Router with one event per missed tick.
                next_at = now + interval if interval is not None else timer["next_at"]
                c.execute(
                    "UPDATE superagent_timers SET occurrence=?,next_at=?,enabled=? WHERE id=?",
                    (occurrence, next_at, int(interval is not None), timer["id"]),
                )
            return triggers

    def _path(self, relative_path):
        candidate = Path(relative_path)
        root = self.store.workspace.root
        if (
            candidate.is_absolute()
            or not candidate.parts
            or any(part in {".", ".."} for part in candidate.parts)
        ):
            raise DomainError("File watch must use a workspace relative path")
        if any(
            part.lower().startswith(".env") or part.lower() in {".git", ".codex", ".ssh"}
            for part in candidate.parts
        ):
            raise DomainError("File watch cannot inspect protected configuration")
        path = root / candidate
        for part in (path, *path.parents):
            if part == root.parent:
                break
            if part.is_symlink() or (getattr(part, "is_junction", lambda: False)()):
                raise DomainError("File watch does not follow links")
        resolved = path.resolve()
        database = Path(self.store.path).resolve()
        if not resolved.is_relative_to(root) or resolved in {
            database,
            Path(str(database) + "-wal"),
            Path(str(database) + "-shm"),
        }:
            raise DomainError("File watch path is protected or outside workspace")
        return path

    def _snapshot(self, relative_path):
        path = self._path(relative_path)
        if not path.exists():
            return "missing", {"path": relative_path, "exists": False}
        if not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size > 1024 * 1024:
            raise DomainError("File watch requires an ordinary file of at most 1 MiB")
        with path.open("rb") as stream:
            content = stream.read(1024 * 1024 + 1)
        self._path(relative_path)
        if len(content) > 1024 * 1024:
            raise DomainError("File watch source grew beyond its ingress limit")
        digest = hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
        return digest, {
            "path": relative_path,
            "exists": True,
            "sha256": digest,
            "size_bytes": len(content),
            "content_base64": base64.b64encode(content).decode("ascii"),
        }

    def watch_file(self, source_id, relative_path, *, thread_key=None, watch_id=None):
        relative_path = str(relative_path)
        fingerprint, _ = self._snapshot(relative_path)
        thread_key = _identifier(thread_key or relative_path, "file Thread")
        watch_id = _identifier(watch_id or new_id("watch"), "file watch ID")
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            c = work.connection
            self._source(c, source_id, "file")
            old = c.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM superagent_file_watches WHERE source_id=? AND relative_path=?",
                (source_id, relative_path),
            ).fetchone()
            if old:
                if old["thread_key"] != thread_key:
                    raise DomainError("File watch identity conflicts with stored Thread")
                return dict(old)
            c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO superagent_file_watches VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,0,NULL,0)",
                (
                    watch_id,
                    source_id,
                    thread_key,
                    relative_path,
                    fingerprint,
                ),
            )
            return dict(
                c.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM superagent_file_watches WHERE id=?", (watch_id,)
                ).fetchone()
            )

    def poll_files(self, *, limit=32):
        if type(limit) is not int or not 1 <= limit <= 256:
            raise DomainError("Invalid file poll limit")
        # Persistent poll order prevents a long watch list from starving files.
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            c = work.connection
            watches = c.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM superagent_file_watches ORDER BY checked_at,id LIMIT ?", (limit,)

tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.
